title: Your money isn't actually in your bank

scenes.text: Your money isn't actually in your bank. Here's what really happens to it.
Mike deposits $1,000. The bank keeps a little, say 10%, and lends $900 to Jake for a car. The dealer deposits that $900... and the bank lends most of it out again.
After just three rounds, accounts show $2,710. But there's still only $1,000 of real cash.
So what if everyone wants their money at once? In March 2023, Silicon Valley Bank customers tried to pull out $42 billion in a single day. The next morning, the bank was shut down.
That's why you need this number. FDIC insurance covers $250,000 per person, per bank, per account type.
Jake's rule: more than $250,000 saved? Split it across banks.
Did you know your bank works like this? Tell me in the comments.

props.disclaimer: Simplified example. US reserve requirement: 0% since 2020. Not financial advice.
